prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When an OAuthClientProvider is reloaded from storage (e.g. after a process restart), the restored token's `token_expiry_time` is never recomputed from `expires_in`, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired token as still valid. This skips the proactive-refresh branch and forces every subsequent expiry into a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When an OAuthClientProvider is reloaded from storage (e.g. after a process restart), the restored token's `token_expiry_time` is never recomputed from `expires_in`, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired token as still valid. This skips the proactive-refresh branch and forces every subsequent expiry into a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the root cause directly in `_initialize` by calling `update_token_expiry` on the loaded tokens (4-line change, drops the `# pragma: no cover` since it's now exercised, and adds an `expired_tokens` test fixture covering the scenario). #2875's own inline comment explicitly names this exact missing-`token_expiry_time` bug as its motivation, but instead of restoring the expiry it papers over the symptom by inserting a whole extra refresh-attempt branch into `async_auth_flow`'s 401 handler (added round trip, larger surface change to a hot path). prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE stream reconnection in _handle_reconnection ultimately fails (max attempts exhausted / underlying error), the pending JSON-RPC request the client is waiting on never gets resolved or gets an opaque failure — both PRs fix this same 'caller hangs after reconnection dies' defect, just via different mechanisms. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE stream reconnection in _handle_reconnection ultimately fails (max attempts exhausted / underlying error), the pending JSON-RPC request the client is waiting on never gets resolved or gets an opaque failure — both PRs fix this same 'caller hangs after reconnection dies' defect, just via different mechanisms. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395's diff is a minimal, self-contained change to the existing exhaustion branch: it reuses already-imported ErrorData/JSONRPCError/INTERNAL_ERROR machinery, adds an isinstance(JSONRPCRequest) guard so notifications aren't sent bogus responses, and removes the stale '# pragma: no cover' since the branch is now exercised — it resolves the specific pending request in-band via a JSON-RPC error tied to that request's id. #3098 takes a more invasive route: a new recursive _unwrap_exception helper to pull a StreamableHTTPError out of an anyio ExceptionGroup and raise it, plus an unrelated __future__ import cleanup bundled into the same diff. Raising an exception out of the reconnection task risks propagating through the enclosing TaskGroup and tearing down the whole client session for what should be a single failed request, rather than cleanly resolving just that request as #2395 does.

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: The stdio write_stream is created with a zero-capacity (rendezvous) memory object stream, which forces a handler to block when it tries to enqueue a new outgoing message (e.g., a final response) while the stdout_writer task is still busy flushing a prior message (e.g., a progress notification). Both PRs address this by changing how the write_stream's buffer size is set. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: The stdio write_stream is created with a zero-capacity (rendezvous) memory object stream, which forces a handler to block when it tries to enqueue a new outgoing message (e.g., a final response) while the stdout_writer task is still busy flushing a prior message (e.g., a progress notification). Both PRs address this by changing how the write_stream's buffer size is set. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2654 changes the default write_stream buffer from 0 to 1, fixing the blocking bug for all callers out of the box, and adds a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the exact progress-notification-blocks-response scenario. 2215 only adds configurable read/write buffer-size parameters but leaves the default at 0, so it does not fix the bug unless a caller explicitly opts in. 2215's diff also targets `anyio.create_memory_object_stream(0)` directly, while both 2552 and 2654 show the surrounding code already refactored to a `create_context_streams[...]` helper — meaning 2215 is based on an older version of stdio.py and would need to be reworked/rebased before it could even apply.

prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WWW-Authenticate header parsing in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py naively split/matched auth-params without respecting quoted-string commas, causing incorrect extraction of fields (e.g. resource_metadata/error) when quoted values contain commas or when the naive regex produced substring matches. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add a quote-aware comma tokenizer to replace the naive splitting/regex logic, but #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the *entire* header into top-level segments and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly filters for the 'Bearer' scheme segment. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only finds the first space and treats everything after it as one param blob, which does not disambiguate between multiple challenges in a single header (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=invalid_token'), a case RFC 7235 permits. #3041's scheme-aware segmentation handles a case #3012's approach does not.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same conditional in `pre_parse_json` (func_metadata.py) that decides whether to `json.loads()` a string input value. The original check `field_info.annotation is not str` triggers JSON-decoding for any non-bare-`str` annotation, including `str | None` unions — so a plain string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", "true", or a JSON-object-looking string) gets silently corrupted into None/int/bool/dict instead of being passed through as a string. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same conditional in `pre_parse_json` (func_metadata.py) that decides whether to `json.loads()` a string input value. The original check `field_info.annotation is not str` triggers JSON-decoding for any non-bare-`str` annotation, including `str | None` unions — so a plain string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "null", "123", "true", or a JSON-object-looking string) gets silently corrupted into None/int/bool/dict instead of being passed through as a string. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` before comparing union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP parameter style `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (Annotated nested inside one arm of a union). #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` checks membership via `arg in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare types `{str, int, float, bool, NoneType}`); an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` arg does not match any of those exactly, so it falls through to `any(arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES ...) -> True` and pre-parsing still runs — leaving the corruption bug live for that common Field-annotated pattern, which is the same shape of parameter this codebase already treats specially elsewhere (see PR #2939's handling of Annotated/Field metadata on other type paths). #2032 does cover more union shapes in the abstract (str|int, str|bool, str|float) but its narrower type-matching approach misses the Annotated case that #3056 targets directly, and #3056's title/scope matches the exact corruption scenario (str|None with JSON-like string values) most concretely.

clusters.pick_reason: #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` before comparing union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP parameter style `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (Annotated nested inside one arm of a union). #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` checks membership via `arg in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare types `{str, int, float, bool, NoneType}`); an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` arg does not match any of those exactly, so it falls through to `any(arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES ...) -> True` and pre-parsing still runs — leaving the corruption bug live for that common Field-annotated pattern, which is the same shape of parameter this codebase already treats specially elsewhere (see PR #2939's handling of Annotated/Field metadata on other type paths). #2032 does cover more union shapes in the abstract (str|int, str|bool, str|float) but its narrower type-matching approach misses the Annotated case that #3056 targets directly, and #3056's title/scope matches the exact corruption scenario (str|None with JSON-like string values) most concretely.

clusters.pick_reason: #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` before comparing union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the idiomatic FastMCP parameter style `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (Annotated nested inside one arm of a union). #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` checks membership via `arg in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare types `{str, int, float, bool, NoneType}`); an `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` arg does not match any of those exactly, so it falls through to `any(arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES ...) -> True` and pre-parsing still runs — leaving the corruption bug live for that common Field-annotated pattern, which is the same shape of parameter this codebase already treats specially elsewhere (see PR #2939's handling of Annotated/Field metadata on other type paths). #2032 does cover more union shapes in the abstract (str|int, str|bool, str|float) but its narrower type-matching approach misses the Annotated case that #3056 targets directly, and #3056's title/scope matches the exact corruption scenario (str|None with JSON-like string values) most concretely.

members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: Both patch the same conditional in `pre_parse_json` (func_metadata.py) that decides whether to `json.loads()` a string input value. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a quote-aware comma tokenizer to replace the naive splitting/regex logic, but #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the *entire* header into top-level segments and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly filters for the 'Bearer' scheme segment. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only finds the first space and treats everything after it as one param blob, which does not disambiguate between multiple challenges in a single header (e.g. 'Basic realm=x, Bearer error=invalid_token'), a case RFC 7235 permits. #3041's scheme-aware segmentation handles a case #3012's approach does not.
